title: \'It was wrong:\' Red Deer dad says Mounties needlessly shot dead mentally ill son
subtitle: A Red Deer man said RCMP officers needlessly killed his mentally-ill, knife-wielding son after efforts to get him help failed.
article: A Red Deer man said he regrets calling RCMP after watching an officer shoot to death his knife-wielding, mentally ill son in what he calls a needless killing.

RCMP said on Thursday afternoon, they responded to a complaint of a person threatening people in a southeast Red Deer home with a knife and ended up fatally shooting a 33-year-old man with a service pistol "when an altercation occurred between the male and the officers ... no officers were physically injured during this incident."

The father of Derek Deon, who was killed, said he was stunned and horrified when three RCMP officers entered his home armed with assault rifles and confronted his son in the younger man\'s basement bedroom.
"They came in and stormed the house, there was no plan," said Vernon Deon.
"It was a complete take-down, it was completely unnecessary."
The man said Derek was in his bed holding a steak knife and was struck with a Taser when he wouldn\'t put the blade down.
His startled son then stumbled off the bed and onto one knee on the floor, still holding the knife when he feared the worst, said Vernon.
"I told them, \'Don\'t shoot\' ... all the officer had to do was back up, he put himself in that position."
He said the encounter lasted only about 30 seconds - his wife Jane estimating up to a minute - and ended with Derek being shot three times by one of the officers.
The officers\' aggressive actions, he said, escalated a situation that could have been handled more slowly and calmly.
"What was the rush? Just calm down - it doesn\'t make any sense. It\'s wrong ... that wasn\'t communicating," said the dad in an anguished voice.
"They wanted to sort it out in 30 seconds after I waited all week (for help for my son)."
He said he and his wife were never physically threatened by Derek on the day he died.

Vernon said the behaviour of his son, who\'d been suffering from schizophrenic spectrum disorder for the past five years, had deteriorated in recent months after he\'d been off his medication and issuing threats against him and his wife and neighbours.
Last week, on April 9 and 11, police had attended his home with Vernon hoping they would take his son to Red Deer Hospital on a mental-health warrant, said the grieving father.
A planned call with a psychiatrist never materialized, he added.

Vernon said he\'d then received a mental-health order for police to use, signed by a provincial court judge on Thursday morning. When Derek verbally threatened his parents again hours later, the dad said he called RCMP, expecting the complaint would finally prompt them to take his son to the hospital.
Instead, he said, when the officers arrived, they "came down like they were going to war."
"It was completely different from anything we\'d seen in dealing with police on these mental-health issues," he said.
In previous instances, RCMP personnel dealing with Derek were a specialized unit augmented with a social worker or mental-health specialist.

But on Thursday, when his son was killed, that unit was apparently busy, said Vernon, who disputed an RCMP press release stating he\'d called with a complaint his son had threatened his parents with a knife.
And he said his son was shot with a rifle, not a handgun, which police say was discharged in the incident.
Derek, he said, was pronounced dead at the scene, despite the efforts of the RCMP officers to save him, said his father.
Said his mother, Jane: "Derek has never been an outright violent person."
Her son, she said, had been admitted to hospital for mental-health reasons "many times," most recently about a year ago.

Alberta RCMP said the law enforcement agency can\'t comment further on the incident or on Vernon\'s allegations, noting the deadly shooting is now under investigation by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team, the province\'s police watchdog agency.

"The Alberta RCMP believes in processes that seek the facts and it\'s important that processes taken to assess the actions of all those involved, including the police, are fair, transparent, and defendable. This is why, as soon as we became aware of this incident, we immediately notified the Director of Law Enforcement and initiated our internal review process," stated the RCMP press release on the incident.
"The Director of Law Enforcement deemed this to be \'in scope\' and has directed ASIRT to investigate."
Vernon said he spoke with ASIRT officials on Thursday following the shooting, adding he can now only wait for the outcome of their investigation.
Derek was a highly artistic person, who loved music and excelled at painting, sculpting and writing, said his father.
But he said his son has struggled with mental-health issues since he was a teen and more recently with substance-abuse challenges amid schizophrenia.
"He talked to people in his mind - he called them his ghost friends - but he was happy," said Vernon.
"I couldn\'t get him the help he needed and I couldn\'t get the police to behave."
